Exception when calling TextPrompt.DefaultValue(value) with brackets
issue.body:
**Information**
 - OS: MacOS
 - Version: 0.46.1.preview.0.8
 - Terminal: iTerm

**Describe the bug**

`TextPrompt.DefaultValue` is not escaped when displayed in TextPrompt.

**To Reproduce**

```cs
  var queryStr = "root['config'][0]";

  AnsiConsole.Prompt(new TextPrompt<string?>("Query: ").DefaultValue(queryStr).AllowEmpty());
```
Exception is thrown: `System.InvalidOperationException: Could not find color or style ''config''.`

Workaround of using `Markup.Escape()` is not suitable as it retains the markup.
```cs
  var result = AnsiConsole.Prompt(new TextPrompt<string?>("Query:").DefaultValue(Markup.Escape(queryStr)).AllowEmpty());
```
Result retains escaping: `root[['config']][[0]]`

A clear and concise description of what the bug is.

**Expected behavior**
DefaultValue is escaped when displayed.

issue.title: Performance regression in `Cell.GetCellLength(string)` via `UnicodeCalculator.GetWidth(string)` on newer TFMs
issue.body:
**Information**
 - OS: Windows
 - Version: 10 22h2
 - Terminal: Windows Terminal

**Describe the bug**

The net10 path of cell measurement `Cell.GetCellLength(string)` uses  `UnicodeCalculator.GetWidth(string)`. This is actually much slower and with more allocations than the net48 path.   I was originally benchmarking to get an idea of how much better the performance ought to have been, given the theoretically more efficient runtime.

There are minor differences in CJK handling in the modern path, so we cannot just roll back to the old handling, but we can reduce allocations in the new path by using the `_runeWidthCache`.

This originally came up as I was trying to demonstrate how much quicker net10 was, but on these specific benchmarks, I found it was much worse:

**before / current main**

| Benchmark                    | .NET 10         | net48          | Penalty        |
|------------------------------|-----------------|----------------|----------------|
| RefreshFrame_DefaultColumns  | 615 µs / 233 KB | 351 µs / 138 KB | net48 2× faster |
| RefreshFrame_DownloadColumns | 1385 µs / 751 KB | 671 µs / 290 KB | net48 2× faster |


**To Reproduce**

BenchmarkDotNet benchmarks already exist, some more focused ones I'll add in my PR.

Switching to net48 TFM I have left outside of the scope of the PR, but here are the steps:

<details>
<summary>Reproducing the .NET Framework (net48) comparison</summary>

The net48 build of the benchmarks consumes Spectre.Console's `netstandard2.0` target.

1. Add `net48` to the benchmark project's target frameworks in `src/Benchmarks/Benchmarks.csproj`:

   ```diff
   -    <TargetFrameworks>net10.0;net9.0;net8.0</TargetFrameworks>
   +    <TargetFrameworks>net10.0;net9.0;net8.0;net48</TargetFrameworks>
   ```

2. Add a net48 job to the benchmark class you want to compare, e.g. in `ProgressBenchmarks.cs`:

   ```diff
    [SimpleJob(RuntimeMoniker.Net10_0)]
   +[SimpleJob(RuntimeMoniker.Net48)]
   ```

3. (Optional, to run a single suite) switch `src/Benchmarks/Program.cs` to the switcher so `--filter` works:

   ```diff
   -        BenchmarkRunner.Run(typeof(Program).Assembly);
   +        BenchmarkSwitcher.FromAssembly(typeof(Program).Assembly).Run(args);
   ```

4. Run from the repo root (the host stays net10.0; BenchmarkDotNet launches the net48 job from the net48 build):

   ```
   dotnet run -c Release -f net10.0 --project src/Benchmarks -- --filter "*ProgressBenchmarks*"
   ```

</details>

**Expected behavior**
Net10 ought to perform much better than net472/net48.

**Additional context**

With the rune width caching, we see a dramatic improvement in time, but more importantly, in allocations:

`TableBenchmarks.Render` — upstream `main` (0acc92f) vs `perf/cell-width-fast-path` (d301b08), paired runs on the same machine (Ryzen 7 3800X, BenchmarkDotNet 0.15.8). Gen0/Gen1/Gen2 are GC counts per 1,000 operations.
`TableBenchmarks.Render` — upstream `main` (0acc92f) vs `perf/cell-width-fast-path` (d301b08), paired runs on the same machine (Ryzen 7 3800X, BenchmarkDotNet 0.15.8). Gen0/Gen1/Gen2 are GC counts per 1,000 operations.

| Runtime  | Rows | Mean (main) | Mean (PR) | Speedup | Allocated (main) | Allocated (PR) | Gen0 (main) | Gen0 (PR) | Gen1 (main) | Gen1 (PR) | Gen2 (main) | Gen2 (PR) |
|----------|-----:|------------:|----------:|--------:|-----------------:|---------------:|------------:|----------:|------------:|----------:|------------:|----------:|
| .NET 8.0 |  100 |    3.613 ms |  0.632 ms |    5.7× |          2.66 MB |         848 KB |       332.0 |     103.5 |       109.4 |      37.1 |           — |         — |
| .NET 9.0 |  100 |    3.375 ms |  0.580 ms |    5.8× |          1.92 MB |         824 KB |       238.3 |     100.6 |        74.2 |      33.2 |           — |         — |
| .NET 10  |  100 |    3.114 ms |  0.586 ms |    5.3× |          1.90 MB |         800 KB |       234.4 |      97.7 |        82.0 |      35.2 |           — |         — |

issue.title: Panel drops or truncates a header that is wider than its content, even with room available
issue.body:
**Information**
 - OS: Linux (Ubuntu 26.04)
 - Version: main @ 0acc92fa
 - Terminal: reproduced with `TestConsole`, so the behaviour is terminal-independent

**Describe the bug**

`Panel.Measure` computes the panel's width from its child content plus the border edges, without considering the header. `AddTopBorder` then renders the header through a `Rule`, which drops or ellipsizes a title that does not fit the width it was given.

The result is that a header wider than the panel's content is silently lost, even when the console has plenty of room. In the first case below the header disappears entirely rather than being truncated.

**To Reproduce**

```csharp
var console = new TestConsole().Width(40);

console.Write(new Panel("x") { Header = new PanelHeader("HDR") });
console.Write(new Panel("Hello World") { Header = new PanelHeader("Configuration Settings") });
```

Actual output on `main` @ 0acc92fa, console width 40:

```
┌───┐
│ x │
└───┘

┌─Configurat…─┐
│ Hello World │
└─────────────┘
```

The first panel has no header at all. The second ellipsizes a 22-character header down to 11 characters despite 40 columns being available.

**Expected behavior**

When the caller has not constrained the width, the panel's natural width should be wide enough to show its own header:

```
┌─HDR─┐
│ x   │
└─────┘

┌─Configuration Settings─┐
│ Hello World            │
└────────────────────────┘
```

Constrained cases should keep collapsing exactly as they do today - an explicit `Width`, `Expand = true`, or a parent that hands down a narrower `maxWidth`. The existing `Render_Header_Collapse` expectation covers that and should not change.

**Additional context**

I have a patch for this and I am happy to open a PR if you want it. Per CONTRIBUTING I am raising the issue first rather than sending an unsolicited PR.

The change is confined to `Panel.Measure`: when `Width` is null and a header is present, the natural maximum grows to the header width plus two border cells and two title-padding cells, clamped to `maxWidth`. Explicit width, `Expand`, and constrained parents are untouched, so only the previously-broken case changes.

Verified against `main` @ 0acc92fa: the full test project goes from 752 passing to 753 passing with the added regression test, and no existing expectation file changes - including `Render_Header_Collapse`, which still produces `┌─Greet…─┐` as before.

Note that this does change rendering for panels whose header is wider than their content: they will render wider than they do today. That is the fix, but it is a visible change and worth calling out.

issue.title: ProgressTask accepts negative MaxValue without validation
Add a feature that allows calendar events to be removed after they have been added
issue.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
If you add a calendar event and make a mistake (e.g. if the end user creates it for the wrong day of the month), you won't be able to remove this entry. The only option is to try to find the event in the CalendarEvents property and delete it. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Provide a method to remove an existing calendar event. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Perhaps it would be possible to allow the programmer to adjust the CalendarEvents property more effectively. 

---
